raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Native single-GPU VAE tiling for Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo evaluates self-attention and convolutions independently within each tile, then blends overlapping outputs. Each position can attend only to that tile's keys and values, and some convolution dependencies are truncated. Native single-GPU tiling is therefore not mathematically equivalent to the untiled VAE, and can produce colored seams.

The default multi-GPU tiling path (`parallel_tiled_decode`) can also produce stitching artifacts. However, multi-GPU decoding also provides a separate `spatial_shard` path: it exchanges convolution halos at each layer and gathers the full spatial features for self-attention, preserving complete spatial dependencies and mathematical equivalence to untiled decoding. This PR therefore replaces only the single-GPU tiling algorithm, leaving the default multi-GPU tiling and `spatial_shard` algorithms unchanged.

The single-GPU text-to-image comparison below uses the same input at 3840×2144. Native tiling can produce grid-like stitching artifacts along horizontal and vertical tile boundaries, visible here as thin purple seams across the tabletop. These visible seams are absent from the untiled and patched outputs. The top row shows full-image previews; the bottom row shows matched crops at 1:1 pixel scale.

![Untiled, native-tiled and patched outputs with matched full-image views and crops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48aa6c17-6909-4ed2-a3ee-c1a639038a21)

## Modifications

This method is enabled only for single-GPU execution. It tiles convolutions by valid output regions before and after global attention, covering both encoding and decoding.

- Partition the pre-attention feature map into disjoint valid regions (cores). Compute each core with its required neighboring halo, then assemble the valid regions into the complete feature map.
- Attention continues to use the native `AttentionBlock`.
- Evaluate subsequent convolutions on the original core grid. Propagate each final output region backwards to derive the required input windows, retain complete halos, crop redundant edges after each stage, and stitch the valid outputs.
- Apply `clamp(-1, 1)` after assembling the valid output regions in single-GPU decoding.

## Accuracy Tests

Seven CPU regressions cover full-versus-tiled encoding and decoding at non-tile-aligned boundaries, output range, single-GPU-only dispatch and native fallback for non-residual architectures.

~~~bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q \
  python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_qwen_image21_attention_barrier.py
~~~

Validation uses Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo on one H20 in BF16: decoding at 1536×1536 and encoding at 1024×1024. Each case has one warmup and three formal calls, using the untiled output for the same input as the tensor-level reference.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single H20, BF16, batch 1, PyTorch 2.14.1/CUDA 13.0, cuDNN 9.24. Component measurements use identical inputs and synchronized wall time, with one warmup and three formal calls per case. Peak GPU memory is measured with PyTorch `max_memory_allocated` and includes the resident VAE and input. Detailed settings, aggregation and individual measurements are in `validation.json` ([validation bundle](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34090707/qwen-image21-single-gpu-tiling-compact-pr-bundle.zip)).

### Encoding

All methods use the same input image. Differences are computed in FP32 across all output channels, and RMSE directly compares the encoded posterior moments with the untiled result.

| Resolution | Method | Time (s) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) | RMSE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024×1024 | Untiled | 0.064 | 1.957 | 0.000000 |
| 1024×1024 | Native tiled | 0.201 | 0.727 | 3.533896 |
| 1024×1024 | Patched | 0.445 | 1.007 | 0.036352 |

### Decoding

All methods use the same latent. Differences are computed in FP32 across all output channels before conversion to 8-bit pixels, and RMSE directly compares the decoded output tensor with the untiled output.

| Resolution | Method | Time (s) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) | RMSE |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1536×1536 | Untiled | 0.650 | 7.607 | 0.000000 |
| 1536×1536 | Native tiled | 1.363 | 0.857 | 0.013966 |
| 1536×1536 | Patched | 1.813 | 0.813 | 0.000897 |

### Full requests

End-to-end inference uses the SGLang Python API: one H20, Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo, BF16, eight steps, guidance 1.0, quality="lossless", default VAE computation optimizations and text-encoder CPU offload.

The text-to-image case produces a 3840×2144 image. The image-to-image case uses three references: the output image and each preprocessed VAE input are 1536×1536, while all three original references are 1024×1024. Each row has one warmup and three formal requests. Time covers the full request and PNG saving; peak memory is sampled through NVML.

Compared with native tiling, the patched end-to-end requests take slightly longer with broadly unchanged peak memory, while restoring mathematical consistency with the untiled VAE and improving output accuracy.

| Request | Method | Time (s) | Peak GPU memory (GiB) | SSIM |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3840×2144 text-to-image | Untiled | 117.05 | 64.54 | 1.000000 |
| 3840×2144 text-to-image | Native tiled | 80.30 | 35.82 | 0.983188 |
| 3840×2144 text-to-image | Patched | 82.66 | 35.78 | 0.999533 |
| 1536×1536 three-reference editing | Untiled | 34.26 | 52.40 | 1.000000 |
| 1536×1536 three-reference editing | Native tiled | 36.71 | 50.35 | 0.720972 |
| 1536×1536 three-reference editing | Patched | 38.66 | 50.61 | 0.996173 |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). N/A: no public API or configuration changes requiring new user documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -661,6 +661,169 @@ def __init__(self, config: QwenImage21VAEConfig, **kwargs):
         if self.spatial_parallel:
             enable_qwen21_spatial_decode(self.decoder)
 
+        # These prerequisites are fixed by the encoder/decoder constructors.
+        self._context_tiles_supported = (
+            (
+                not torch.distributed.is_initialized()
+                or torch.distributed.get_world_size() == 1
+            )
+            and ac.is_residual
+            and ac.patch_size in (None, 1)
+            and self.spatial_compression_ratio == 2 ** (len(ac.dim_mult) - 1)
+        )
+        self._context_stochastic_dropout = 0 < ac.dropout < 1
+
+    def _supports_context_tiles(self, x, *, encode):
+        branch = self.encoder if encode else self.decoder
+        return (
+            self._context_tiles_supported
+            and not (branch.training and self._context_stochastic_dropout)
+            and x.shape[2] == 1
+            and all(n > 0 for n in x.shape[-2:])
+            and (
+                not encode
+                or all(n % self.spatial_compression_ratio == 0 for n in x.shape[-2:])
+            )
+        )
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _context_plan(core, stages, shape):
+        """Back-propagate half-open rectangles through residual/up/conv stages.
+
+        A stage is (module, residual radius, scale): 2 upsamples, -2
+        downsamples, and 1 preserves the grid. Invert the final sampling
+        operation before the residual radius, preserving stride phase and
+        clipping each interval at the true image boundary.
+        """
+        shapes = [shape]
+        for _, _, scale in stages:
+            shapes.append(
+                tuple(n * scale if scale > 0 else n // -scale for n in shapes[-1])
+            )
+        plan = [core]
+        for (_, radius, scale), size in zip(reversed(stages), reversed(shapes[:-1])):
+            previous = []
+            for (lo, hi), length in zip(plan[-1], size):
+                if scale == 2:
+                    lo, hi = (lo - 1) // 2, hi // 2 + 1
+                elif scale == -2:
+                    lo, hi = 2 * lo, 2 * hi + 1
+                lo, hi = lo - radius, hi + radius
+                if scale == -2:
+                    # Preserve the global stride phase and the even local size
+                    # required by the AvgDown3D shortcut at this stage.
+                    lo, hi = lo // 2 * 2, -(-hi // 2) * 2
+                previous.append((max(0, lo), min(length, hi)))
+            plan.append(tuple(previous))
+        return list(reversed(plan))
+
+    def _context_prefix(self, source, window, *, encode):
+        branch = self.encoder if encode else self.decoder
+        stages = [(branch.conv_in, 1, 1)]
+        if encode:
+            stages += [
+                (
+                    block,
+                    2 * len(block.resnets),
+                    -2 if block.downsampler is not None else 1,
+                )
+                for block in branch.down_blocks
+            ]
+        stages.append((branch.mid_block.resnets[0], 2, 1))
+        plan = self._context_plan(window, stages, tuple(source.shape[-2:]))
+        if encode:
+            ratio = self.spatial_compression_ratio
+            plan[0] = tuple(
+                (a // ratio * ratio, min(n, -(-b // ratio) * ratio))
+                for (a, b), n in zip(plan[0], source.shape[-2:])
+            )
+        (top, bottom), (left, right) = plan[0]
+        x = source[..., top:bottom, left:right]
+        if not encode:
+            x = self.post_quant_conv(x)
+        for index, (block, _, scale) in enumerate(stages):
+            x = block(x)
+            (top, _), (left, _) = plan[index]
+            if scale == -2:
+                top, left = top // 2, left // 2
+            (a, b), (c, d) = plan[index + 1]
+            x = x[..., a - top : b - top, c - left : d - left].contiguous()
+        return x
+
+    def _context_tiled(self, source, *, encode):
+        branch = self.encoder if encode else self.decoder
+        ratio = self.spatial_compression_ratio
+        shape = tuple(n // ratio if encode else n for n in source.shape[-2:])
+        _, _, step_h, step_w = self._spatial_tile_geometry()
+        if step_h <= 0 or step_w <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("VAE tile strides must be positive")
+        cores = [
+            ((top, min(top + step_h, shape[0])), (left, min(left + step_w, shape[1])))
+            for top in range(0, shape[0], step_h)
+            for left in range(0, shape[1], step_w)
+        ]
+        # Assemble each valid prefix core once. The native attention block sees
+        # the complete spatial grid, with no query or key/value partitioning.
+        context = None
+        for (top, bottom), (left, right) in cores:
+            tile = self._context_prefix(
+                source, ((top, bottom), (left, right)), encode=encode
+            )
+            if context is None:
+                context = tile.new_empty((*tile.shape[:-2], *shape))
+            context[..., top:bottom, left:right] = tile
+        del tile
+        context = branch.mid_block.attentions[0](context)
+        stages = [(branch.mid_block.resnets[1], 2, 1)]
+        if not encode:
+            stages += [
+                (block, 2 * len(block.resnets), 2 if block.upsampler is not None else 1)
+                for block in branch.up_blocks
+            ]
+        stages.append((None, 1, 1))  # pointwise norm/SiLU, then conv_out
+        output_scale = 1 if encode else ratio
+        output = None
+        for core in cores:
+            target = tuple((a * output_scale, b * output_scale) for a, b in core)
+            plan = self._context_plan(target, stages, shape)
+            (top, bottom), (left, right) = plan[0]
+            x = context[..., top:bottom, left:right].contiguous()
+            # Resume the original core grid after the attention barrier. Include
+            # the complete suffix halo, then discard dead halo at each stage.
+            for index, (block, _, scale) in enumerate(stages):
+                if block is None:
+                    x = branch.conv_out(branch.nonlinearity(branch.norm_out(x)))
+                elif isinstance(block, QwenImage21ResidualUpBlock):
+                    x = block(x, first_chunk=True)
+                else:
+                    x = block(x)
+                (top, _), (left, _) = plan[index]
+                (a, b), (c, d) = plan[index + 1]
+                x = x[
+                    ...,
+                    a - top * scale : b - top * scale,
+                    c - left * scale : d - left * scale,
+                ].contiguous()
+            if encode:
+                x = self.quant_conv(x)
+            if output is None:
+                output = x.new_empty(
+                    (*x.shape[:-2], shape[0] * output_scale, shape[1] * output_scale)
+                )
+            (a, b), (c, d) = target
+            output[..., a:b, c:d] = x
+        return output
+
+    def spatial_tiled_encode(self, x):
+        if not self._supports_context_tiles(x, encode=True):
+            return super().spatial_tiled_encode(x)
+        return self._context_tiled(x, encode=True)
+
+    def spatial_tiled_decode(self, z):
+        if not self._supports_context_tiles(z, encode=False):
+            return super().spatial_tiled_decode(z)
+        return self._context_tiled(z, encode=False).clamp(-1, 1)
+
     def _encode(self, x):
         if x.shape[2] != 1:
             raise ValueError("Qwen-Image 2.1 VAE expects one image frame")

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""CPU regressions for single-GPU Qwen-Image-2.1 VAE tiling."""
+
+from unittest.mock import Mock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.configs.models.vaes.qwenimage21 import (
+    QwenImage21VAEArchConfig,
+    QwenImage21VAEConfig,
+)
+from sglang.multimodal_gen.runtime.models.vaes import autoencoder_kl_qwenimage21 as q
+
+
+def tiny_vae(**arch_overrides):
+    torch.manual_seed(42)
+    arch = dict(
+        in_channels=3,
+        base_dim=2,
+        decoder_base_dim=2,
+        z_dim=2,
+        dim_mult=(1, 2, 4, 8, 8),
+        num_res_blocks=2,
+        is_residual=True,
+    )
+    arch.update(arch_overrides)
+    model = (
+        q.AutoencoderKLQwenImage21(
+            QwenImage21VAEConfig(
+                arch_config=QwenImage21VAEArchConfig(**arch),
+                use_tiling=True,
+                use_temporal_tiling=False,
+                use_parallel_tiling=False,
+            )
+        )
+        .double()
+        .eval()
+    )
+    ratio = model.spatial_compression_ratio
+    model.tile_sample_min_height = 24 * ratio
+    model.tile_sample_min_width = 32 * ratio
+    model.tile_sample_stride_height = 16 * ratio
+    model.tile_sample_stride_width = 19 * ratio
+    return model
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encode", [True, False], ids=["encoder", "decoder"])
+def test_context_tiles_match_untiled_output(encode):
+    model = tiny_vae()
+    # Neither axis ends on a tile boundary; compare the complete output.
+    shape = (1, 3, 1, 512, 608) if encode else (1, 2, 1, 23, 26)
+    source = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.float64)
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        expected = model._encode(source) if encode else model._decode(source)
+        actual = model.encode(source).parameters if encode else model.decode(source)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=5e-9, atol=2e-10)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("world_size", [1, 2])
+def test_context_tiling_is_single_process_only(monkeypatch, world_size):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.distributed, "is_initialized", lambda: True)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(torch.distributed, "get_world_size", lambda: world_size)
+    model = tiny_vae()
+    marker = torch.tensor([0.375])
+    context = Mock(return_value=marker)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(model, "_context_tiled", context)
+    for encode in (True, False):
+        name = "spatial_tiled_encode" if encode else "spatial_tiled_decode"
+        native = Mock(return_value=marker)
+        monkeypatch.setattr(q.ParallelTiledVAE, name, native)
+        shape = (1, 3, 1, 64, 80) if encode else (1, 2, 1, 3, 4)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(getattr(model, name)(torch.zeros(shape)), marker)
+        assert native.call_count == int(world_size > 1)
+    assert context.call_count == (2 if world_size == 1 else 0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encode", [True, False], ids=["encoder", "decoder"])
+def test_nonresidual_architecture_keeps_native_tiling(encode):
+    model = tiny_vae(is_residual=False)
+    shape = (1, 3, 1, 64, 80) if encode else (1, 2, 1, 3, 4)
+    source = torch.randn(shape, dtype=torch.float64)
+    name = "spatial_tiled_encode" if encode else "spatial_tiled_decode"
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        expected = getattr(q.ParallelTiledVAE, name)(model, source)
+        actual = getattr(model, name)(source)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0)
+
+
+def test_tiled_decode_preserves_output_range():
+    model = tiny_vae()
+    with torch.inference_mode():
+        model.decoder.conv_out.weight.zero_()
+        model.decoder.conv_out.bias.fill_(2.0)
+        actual = model.decode(torch.zeros((1, 2, 1, 25, 34), dtype=torch.float64))
+    assert torch.equal(actual, torch.ones_like(actual))
